_schema.key: match a feature by name (as spelled in geo-world.json / geo-us.json) or by its numeric id
_schema.races: [{ office, next, pick, enthusiasm, note?, tier?, rank? }] — one entry per contest
_schema.office: what's being contested — free text; the tier is read off it
_schema.tier: optional override: executive | legislature | governor. Otherwise inferred from the office name
_schema.rank: optional number that overrides the computed rank outright — last resort when the office keywords sort a race wrongly
_schema.next: ISO date of the election, or null if unscheduled
_schema.pick: who i'd support — free text. 'none' is a real answer
_schema.past: [{ date, office, pick, enthusiasm, note }] — earlier reads, oldest first. A held race lands in the history on its own; entries here are for saying something the standing entry did not
_schema.logged: ISO date the endorsement was made — stamped by scripts/politics/stamp-logged.py when the pick changes, not hand-written. Changing enthusiasm on the same pick leaves it alone
_schema._priority: Soonest race leads — it colours the map and heads the overlay. Rank only settles a shared date: executive (president/PM/chancellor) > legislature > governor. Within the legislature, the US ranks senate above house; parliamentary systems rank the lower house (commons/bundestag/lok sabha) above the upper.
